data.narrative:
Mazama, a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Sriram Vasantharajan, has raised $30M+ to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises 9 peer companies, including 1 public (LNZA) and 8 private entities such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables—fewer than three datapoints survive narrow filtering—rendering a peer-median approach unreliable for valuation triangulation.

A stage-progression methodology is applicable here. Using the $30M total raised as a valuation proxy for Series A, a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier to the next financing stage implies a valuation of $60M. This multiplier reflects typical Series A venture capital dynamics and serves as the sole quantitative anchor in the absence of robust peer multiples.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $51M to $69M, centered on a $60M median. This range reflects reasonable variance around the stage-progression result but rests on a single method, creating material sensitivity to the assumed step-up multiplier. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer comparables, limited visibility into Mazama's unit economics and market traction, and broad dispersion in valuation multiples across the fragmented Climate & Energy sector. Additional operational and commercial data would strengthen conviction in this range.
